Premera Blue Cross Blue Shield of Alaska  
Attn: Member Appeals  
P.O. Box 91102  
Seattle, WA 98111-9202  
Fax: 425-918-5592

Re: Appeal of denial of total shoulder arthroplasty  
Member: Taylor Lawson  
Member ID: W261288012  
Reference number: POC-F781755028-57061  
Procedure: Total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472  
Treating surgeon: Marchetti, MD

Dear Member Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472. Please conduct a complete reconsideration using the enclosed clinical records.

The applicable Premera policy is MEDICAL POLICY – 7.01.590 Shoulder Arthroplasty, policy number 7.01.590, effective April 1, 2026, and last revised March 23, 2026. The policy states:

“Total shoulder arthroplasty may be considered medically necessary for joint disease when ALL of the following criteria are met:”

The clinical records address those criteria as follows:

1. Documented joint disease

The prior authorization records document destructive degenerative disease of the shoulder. Radiographs obtained on June 15, 2026, show complete loss of the glenohumeral joint space, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and a flattened glenoid. Please also consider Dr. Marchetti’s documented diagnosis of [insert exact diagnosis from the surgeon’s clinical note, if needed].

The policy lists the following qualifying diagnoses:

“There is a documented diagnosis of one of the following:  
o Degenerative joint disease (DJD)  
o Osteoarthritis (OA)  
o Rheumatoid arthritis (RA)  
o Traumatic arthritis  
o Avascular necrosis”

2. Pain and functional disability

The patient has had 12 months of progressive shoulder pain that has not been relieved by rest. The condition causes substantial functional impairment: the patient cannot reach overhead, cannot dress without help, and cannot sleep on the affected side. Examination shows glenohumeral crepitus, active forward elevation limited to 90 degrees, and external rotation limited to 10 degrees.

These records address the policy requirement that treatment be needed because of:

“Disabling pain for at least 3 months duration”

or:

“Functional disability which interferes with the ability to carry out activities of daily living for at least 3 months duration”

The documented 12-month symptom history and inability to perform dressing and overhead activities substantially exceed the three-month duration requirement.

3. Imaging findings

The June 15, 2026, shoulder radiographs show complete loss of the glenohumeral joint space, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and a flattened glenoid. The CT scan confirms an intact rotator cuff.

The policy requires:

“Radiographic or imaging evidence (e.g., X-ray, CT, MRI) of destructive degenerative joint disease of the shoulder in the 12 months prior to surgery as evidenced by ONE or more of the following:  
o Irregular joint surfaces  
o Glenoid sclerosis  
o Glenoid osteophyte changes  
o Flattened glenoid  
o Cystic changes in the humeral head  
o Joint space narrowing”

The imaging documents at least three of the listed findings: glenoid sclerosis, glenoid osteophyte changes, and a flattened glenoid. It also documents complete loss of the glenohumeral joint space.

4. Failed conservative treatment

The patient completed eight weeks of supervised physical therapy from May 3, 2026, through June 28, 2026, including 18 visits focused on range of motion and periscapular strengthening. The physical therapy discharge note documents this treatment.

The patient also used NSAIDs for eight months with inadequate relief. An intra-articular corticosteroid injection on April 28, 2026, provided only three weeks of partial relief.

The policy requires:

“Documentation of three months of failed non-operative conservative management as demonstrated by a trial of one or more of the following:  
o Anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics  
o Intra-articular injection of corticosteroids as appropriate”

The patient’s eight months of NSAID treatment and corticosteroid injection address this requirement. The policy also requires:

“A 6 week trial of one or more of the following physical measures under the direction of a healthcare professional:  
o Physical therapy  
o Activity modification  
o Flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises”

The patient completed eight weeks and 18 visits of supervised physical therapy, exceeding the six-week physical-treatment requirement.

5. Absence of listed contraindicating conditions

The records do not document active infection, and the patient is a non-smoker with a BMI of 29. The clinical summary also documents no untreated substance use. Please review the medical records for confirmation that none of the policy’s listed exclusions or contraindications apply.

The policy states that total shoulder arthroplasty is not medically necessary when the criteria are not met and separately lists conditions including active joint infection, active systemic bacteremia, active skin infection or an open wound at the surgical site, inadequate bone stock, deltoid deficiency, and neuropathic or paralytic shoulder disorders. The submitted records instead document an intact rotator cuff and do not identify any of those conditions.

Based on the documented diagnosis, 12 months of disabling pain and functional limitation, imaging-confirmed destructive glenohumeral disease, eight months of unsuccessful NSAID treatment, limited response to corticosteroid injection, and more than six weeks of supervised physical therapy, the requested total shoulder arthroplasty meets the applicable medical-necessity requirements.

Please reverse the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 23472. If Premera continues to deny the request, please provide the specific criterion determined not to be satisfied, identify the clinical information relied upon, and provide the complete clinical review rationale.

Please include the attached clinical records in the appeal file:

- June 15, 2026, shoulder radiographs and report
- CT imaging and report
- Physical therapy discharge note documenting 18 visits from May 3, 2026, through June 28, 2026
- Medication and injection history
- Dr. Marchetti’s clinical evaluation and treatment recommendation
- Any additional records supporting the diagnosis and planned procedure

Sincerely,

Taylor Lawson
